visual.title: The three CARS skills
visual.alt: Three bands, one per AAMC skill. Skill 1, Foundations of Comprehension, 30 percent: AAMC's sub-skills are understanding the basic components of the text and inferring meaning or intent from immediate sentence context; signal stems include the central thesis is, according to the passage, and as used in paragraph 3 X most nearly means; the move is to go back to the text. Skill 2, Reasoning Within the Text, 30 percent: integrating distant components of the text to infer an author's message, intent, purpose, belief, position, bias or assumptions, and recognizing and evaluating arguments and their structural elements; stems include it can be inferred, the author implies, and X is mentioned primarily in order to; the move is to analyse how the argument is built. Skill 3, Reasoning Beyond the Text, 40 percent: applying or extrapolating ideas to new contexts, and assessing the impact of new factors or information on passage ideas; stems include the author would most likely respond, most analogous to, and if true would most strengthen or weaken; the move is to use the passage as a lens on new information. A footer notes that errors cascade upward and that the passage, not prior knowledge, decides the answer.
